options: As soon as the plane landed, I called Mom
The plane didn't land, and I called Mom
Sometime after landing I'll call Mom
items.explanation: iner inmez — the moment it landed. Like English “no sooner”: a minus that denies nothing. It means “right away.”

options: In the morning I don't wake up without coffee
In the morning, as soon as I wake up, I drink coffee
In the morning I drink coffee so I don't fall asleep
items.explanation: uyanır uyanmaz — as soon as I wake up. The habit is in the main verb içerim.

options: Before we even got to the hotel, we ran to the sea
As soon as we got to the hotel, we ran to the sea
We'll get to the hotel and run to the sea
items.explanation: varır varmaz — as soon as we got there. The past shows in koştuk.

options: As soon as you get home, text me
Don't text me until you get there
I texted as soon as I got there
items.explanation: Same pair, and yaz is a request. So: as soon as you get home — text me.

exercises.instruction: What tail does the first click get?

items.explanation: Stem ends in a vowel → -r. One syllable → -ar/-er. Longer stems and exceptions like gel-, al- → -ır/-ir/-ur/-ür.

items.translation: The moment the movie started, he fell asleep.
items.explanation: The pair is in the aorist: başlar başlamaz. The past is only in uyudu.
English says “as soon as I got home” — past. The Turkish pair stays timeless: gelir gelmez. The past is already in uyudum.

items.translation: As soon as she heard the news, she burst into tears.
items.explanation: duy- is one syllable, not an exception: duyar duymaz.

exercises.instruction: Office dominoes: pick the pair so the second event happens right away
exercises.description: Two events as domino tiles. The learner picks one of three -(A/I)r ... -mAz pairs, the tiles fall, the sentence builds. Logic lives in index.html.

items.ru: The meeting ended — Ali left right away.
items.explanation: bit- is one syllable: biter, then the minus bitmez.

items.ru: The bus came — we got on right away.
items.explanation: Plus first, then minus, no tense: gelir gelmez. English “came” doesn’t go into the pair.

items.ru: He saw me — and waved right away.
items.explanation: gör- is an exception: görür. The minus is görmez.

items.ru: As soon as the guests leave, we're going straight to bed.
items.explanation: git- is one syllable: gider, t → d. The pair has no person.

items.ru: I opened the door — and right away saw the cat.
items.explanation: aç- is one syllable: açar açmaz. The past is only in gördüm.

items.ru: As soon as you get paid, pay back the debt.
items.explanation: al- is one of the thirteen exceptions: alır almaz.

exercises.instruction: Say it yourself: fill in the missing part

items.translation: In the morning, as soon as I wake up, I drink coffee.
items.explanation: uyan- is longer than one syllable: uyanır. The last vowel is a → -ır (ı = the a in “about”).

items.translation: As soon as you get home, text me!
items.explanation: var- is an exception: varır varmaz.

items.translation: The moment class ended, they went outside.
items.explanation: The second click is the same verb with a minus: bitmez.

items.prompt: How do you say: “As soon as exams were over, we went on vacation”?
items.explanation: The pair biter bitmez, the past is in çıktık.

items.statement: Like English “as soon as I got home,” the pair can take the past: “geldim gelmedim.”
items.explanation: No. English puts the past in both clauses, Turkish doesn’t: gelir gelmez is timeless. The past goes only in the main verb.

items.translation: As soon as it started raining, we went into a café.
items.explanation: başla- ends in a vowel: just -r — başlar.

items.prompt: How is “Ders bitince” different from “Ders biter bitmez”?
items.explanation: -ince means “when,” time can pass. -ir -mez — zero seconds.

items.prompt: What's the pair for the verb otur-?
items.explanation: otur- is longer than one syllable: oturur, the minus is oturmaz.
